chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim from Ibrahim from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

"Beware of killing all beasts, and do not touch anything of the perfume or the oil while in your state of Ihram. Beware of the perfume in your provisions, and hold your nose against the good scent, but do not hold it against the foul smell, for it is not proper to delight in a good scent. So whoever is tested by any of that, upon him is its Ghusl (ritual bath), and he should give charity in proportion to what he did."

key_terms.إِحْرَامٌ: The state of ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah

ai.seo_question: What are the prohibitions and expiations for a pilgrim in Ihram regarding scents and killing animals?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) details the sensory restrictions of Ihram, emphasizing the preservation of natural scent and the avoidance of deliberate pleasure derived from perfumes or oils. It establishes a clear legal framework where violation incurs both a ritual purification (Ghusl) and a proportional charitable expiation (Kaffarah), reflecting the Shia emphasis on balancing spiritual humility with practical legal obligations.
